properties.name: The reply-shape fallback flips from signpost to duplicate, so an unmeasured client — which every connector is — gets the payload
properties.rationale:
Anthony, 2026-09-21: "go with your recommendation", on a recommended order of connector work whose first item was this default. It is the only item on flo2's own corrected connector list (F28) with an OBSERVED failure behind it.

WHY THE FALLBACK IS THE WHOLE POINT. The rule is keyed on the handshake NAME and no automatic detection is possible — `dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer` establishes that the negotiated protocol revision is uncorrelated with whether a client READS `structuredContent`, because Grok negotiated the newest revision reflow2 has ever seen and still dropped the field. A name-keyed rule cannot learn, so the fallback is the branch every UNMEASURED client takes — and every connector is unmeasured by construction. It was `Signpost`, which flo2 measured as failing both populations at once: a content-only reader gets one useless sentence, and an empty-fallback reader is defeated by the block being non-empty.

WHY IT IS NOT A BLANKET FLIP, which is the part worth not losing. `claude-code` reads the structured half and is the daily driver here; duplicating every payload into its text block would double the bytes for no reader. So the change inverts the DEFAULT and turns the measured readers into an explicit list. The match on `claude-code` is narrow on purpose — `claude-ai` and any other Claude surface are unmeasured connectors and must fall through — and a test requires the two to differ, because adding a name on a guess would re-create the defect for that client quietly.

THE BOUNDING CONSTRAINT HOLDS. The 2026-08-23 decision that created the signpost was driven by a 157,785-byte `detect_gaps` reply that a harness refused. Since `reply_budget` every JSON reply is capped at 30,000 characters, so the worst case is twice a BOUNDED reply, and `req:never-silently-absent` is satisfied because `duplicate` is never empty.

OBSERVED FAILING AT BOTH LAYERS BEFORE THE CHANGE. The unit test was run red against the old code. For the wire case, a binary was built from the pre-change tree and kept aside; all three unmeasured names returned the signpost sentence against it, and the payload against the new one. That mattered: `tools/test_content_policy.py` already covered `--content-policy duplicate` for an unnamed client, which proves the OVERRIDE and never the DEFAULT — so the branch every connector actually takes had no wire coverage at all.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether Grok should move to `empty`, and whether one shape should serve every client. Both wait on the headless Grok probe, and the decision node stays `proposed` for that reason.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `by_client_name`'s else-branch returns `Duplicate` instead of `Signpost`, and the clients measured to read `structuredContent` (`claude-code`, and this repo's own `smoke_mcp` harness) are now named explicitly so they keep the signpost and pay nothing. `grok*` → duplicate and `*opencode*` → empty are unchanged. `tools/test_content_policy.py` gains a wire case for three unmeasured names with NO flag; `content_policy.rs` gains two unit tests, one requiring the unmeasured default and one requiring `claude-code` to differ from `claude-ai`.
